car.name: Goldilocks 1955
car.description: Stirling Moss / Denis Jenkinson, 1 May 1955 Mille Miglia-winning Mercedes-Benz 300 SLR #722 inspiration. Open two-seat W196 S racer, 2982 cc injected inline-eight, rear drive and five-speed. Original teal/copper art; estimated event setup, not a road 300 SL or Uhlenhaut coupe.

catalogProvenance.referenceVehicle: Stirling Moss / Denis Jenkinson, Mercedes-Benz 300 SLR W196 S #722, winner of the Mille Miglia on 1 May 1955. Open two-seat competition car, not road 300 SL, Uhlenhaut coupe or modern SLR McLaren.

sources.access: Mercedes museum account of original #722 establishes 1 May 1955, 07:22 start, Moss/Jenkinson victory, pure competition W196 S architecture, M196 S inline-eight and 203 kW/276 PS continuous rating at 7000 RPM; no original speedometer. Two headrest fairings, right side exhaust and route-book cockpit details inform art.

Primary Daimler-Benz press packet dated 26 April 1955, archived by third party: 2982 cc injected desmodromic inline-eight, dry sump, mechanical five-speed, rear transaxle, drum brakes, 6.00-16 front/7.00-16 rear race tires, about 810 kg dry excluding fuel/water/oil. Not event running mass.
Manufacturer history confirms winning crew and record 10:07:48 at 157.65 km/h average.

verifiedFacts.trim: Mercedes-Benz 300 SLR W196 S open two-seat competition racer
verifiedFacts.engine: M196 S 2982 cc injected naturally aspirated inline-eight

estimates: Power uses the Mercedes museum continuous 203 kW rating, not a claim of event-day maximum dyno output or generic later 310 PS. 1050 kg running mass, 235 lb-ft peak torque, full curve, geometry, 170 mph/6-second 0-60 targets, ratios/final drive, suspension, aero, brake tuning and 200 L fuel capacity are simulation estimates. Historical 810 kg is dry without fuel, water or oil, not imported as running weight.

Equal 175/80R16 tires approximate historical staggered crossply 6.00-16/7.00-16. Native generic suspension/brake physics do not reproduce swing-axle geometry, drum fade, desmodromic actuation, dry sump or exact fuel-load changes. Auto Assist is accessibility, not a factory automatic; no ABS/TC by default.

Original teal/copper/cream open body and aluminum/check-cloth cockpit, not historic silver/red number livery or copied logos. Digital speed/RPM/gear/fuel, shared wheel and generic engine audio are game conventions; original #722 had no speedometer. Route-scroll box and pedal arrangement are artistic approximations. Car-scoped wiper mounts are empty for the open windscreen, avoiding floating wipers without shared renderer changes. Source PNGs preserved; decoded wheel opacity normalization only.
